C. Reset of Floating Interest Rate on EMI based Personal Loans

310.The following instructions shall be applicable to the existing as well as new personal loans with effect from January 1, 2024. An RCB shall put in place an appropriate policy framework meeting the following requirements for implementation and compliance:

(1) At the time of sanction, the RCB shall clearly communicate to the borrower about the possible impact of change in benchmark interest rate on the loan leading to changes in EMI and / or tenor or both. Subsequently, any increase in the EMI / tenor or both on account of the above shall be communicated to the borrower immediately through appropriate channels.

(2) At the time of reset of interest rates, the RCB may, at its option, provide a choice to the borrower to switch over to a fixed rate as per its Board approved policy. The policy, inter alia, may also specify the number of times a borrower will be allowed to switch during the tenor of the loan.

(3) The borrowers shall also be given the choice to opt for (i) enhancement in EMI or elongation of tenor or for a combination of both options; and, (ii) to prepay, either in part or in full, at any point during the tenor of the loan. Levy of pre-payment charges shall be subject to extant instructions.

Note: Whenever there is a reset of interest rates for an entire class of borrowers in a particular loan category, say home loan, due to increase in the reference benchmark; the RCB shall provide the following options to the borrowers:

(i) Either enhancement in EMI or elongation of number of EMIs, keeping the EMI unchanged or a combination of both options;

(ii) Switch to fixed interest rate for the remaining portion of the loan, where such an option is provided by the RCB; and

(iii) To prepay, either in part or in full, at any point during the residual tenor of the loan.

(4) All applicable charges for switching of loans from floating to fixed rate and any other service charges / administrative costs incidental to the exercise of the above options shall be transparently disclosed in the sanction letter and also at the time of revision of such charges / costs by the RCB from time to time. The applicable charges shall be as approved by the Board and shall be displayed on the RCB’s website.

(5) The RCB shall ensure that the elongation of tenor in case of floating rate loan does not result in negative amortisation.

(6) The RCB shall share / make accessible to the borrower, through appropriate channels, a statement at the end of each quarter which shall at the minimum, enumerate the principal and interest recovered till date, EMI amount, number of EMIs left and annualized rate of interest / APR for the entire tenor of the loan. The RCB shall ensure that the statements are simple and easily understood by the borrower.

311.Apart from the EMI based loans, these instructions shall also apply, mutatis mutandis, to all equated instalment-based personal loans of different periodicities irrespective of whether they are linked to an external benchmark or an internal benchmark. In case of personal loans linked to an external benchmark, the RCB shall put in place adequate information systems to monitor transmission of changes in the benchmark rate to the lending rate.

D. Pre-payment Charges on Loans

312. In case of existing floating rate term loans sanctioned to individual borrowers on or before December 31, 2025, an RCB shall not levy pre-payment charges.

313. An RCB shall adhere to the following directions regarding levy of pre-payment charges on loans and advances (term loans as well as demand loans) sanctioned or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.

(1) For all floating rate loans granted for purposes other than business to individuals, with or without co-obligant(s), an RCB shall not levy pre-payment charges.

(2) For all floating rate loans with sanctioned amount / limit up to ₹50 lakh granted for business purpose to individuals and Micro and Small Enterprises (as defined in Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006), with or without co-obligant(s), an RCB shall not levy pre-payment charges.

(3) The Directions at paragraph 313(1) and 313(2) above shall be applicable irrespective of the source of funds used for pre-payment of loans, either in part or in full, and without any minimum lock-in period.

(4) Applicability of above Directions for dual / special rate (combination of fixed and floating rate) loans will depend on whether the loan is on floating rate at the time of pre-payment.

(5) In cases other than those mentioned at paragraphs 313(1) and 313(2) above, pre-payment charges, if any, shall be as per the approved policy of the RCB. However, in case of term loans, pre-payment charges, if levied by the RCB, shall be based on the amount being prepaid. In case of cash credit/ overdraft facilities, pre-payment charges on closure of the facility before the due date shall be levied on an amount not exceeding the sanctioned limit.

(6) In case of cash credit / overdraft facilities, no pre-payment charges shall be applicable if the borrower intimates the RCB of her / his its intention not to renew the facility before the period as stipulated in the loan agreement, provided that the facility gets closed on the due date.

(7) An RCB shall not levy any charges where pre-payment is effected at the instance of the RCB.

(8) The applicability or otherwise of pre-payment charges shall be clearly disclosed in the sanction letter and loan agreement. Further, in case of loans and advances where KFS is to be provided as specified in paragraph 309 above, the same shall also be mentioned in the KFS. No pre-payment charges which have not been disclosed as specified herein shall be charged by the RCB.

(9) The RCB shall not levy any charges / fees retrospectively at the time of pre-payment of loans, which were waived off earlier by it.

E. Release of Movable / Immovable Property Documents on Repayment/ Settlement of Personal Loans

314. An RCB shall release all the original movable / immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry within a period of 30 days after full repayment/ settlement of the loan account.

315. The borrower shall be given the option of collecting the original movable / immovable property documents either from the banking outlet / branch where the loan account was serviced or any other office of the RCB where the documents are available, as per her / his preference.

316. The timeline and place of return of original movable / immovable property documents shall be mentioned in the loan sanction letters issued on or after December 1, 2023.

317. In order to address the contingent event of demise of the sole borrower or joint borrowers, the RCB shall have a well laid out procedure for return of original movable / immovable property documents to the legal heirs. Such procedure shall be displayed on the website of the RCB along with other similar policies and procedures for customer information.

E.1 Compensation for delay in release of Property Documents

318. An RCB shall communicate to the borrower reasons for delay in releasing of original movable / immovable property documents or failing to file charge satisfaction form with relevant registry beyond 30 days after full repayment/ settlement of loan. In case where the delay is attributable to the RCB, it shall compensate the borrower at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay.

319. In case of loss / damage to original movable / immovable property documents, either in part or in full, the RCB shall assist the borrower in obtaining duplicate / certified copies of the movable / immovable property documents and shall bear the associated costs, in addition to paying compensation as indicated at paragraph 318 above. However, in such cases, an additional time of 30 days will be available to the RCB to complete this procedure and the delayed period penalty will be calculated thereafter (i.e., after a total period of 60 days).

320. The instructions contained under this section shall be applicable to all cases where release of original movable / immovable property documents falls due on or after December 1, 2023. Further, the compensation provided under these directions shall be without prejudice to the rights of a borrower to get any other compensation as per any applicable law.

F. Release of other assets of the deceased borrowers to their legal heirs

321. An RCB shall not insist upon legal representation for release of other assets of deceased borrowers irrespective of the amount involved. The RCB may, however, call for succession certificates from legal heirs of deceased borrowers in cases where there are disputes and all legal heirs do not join in indemnifying the RCB or in certain other exceptional cases where the RCB has a reasonable doubt about the genuineness of the claimant(s) being the only legal heir(s) of the borrower.

G. Conduct related aspects in Lending Against Gold and Silver Collateral

322. The Directions contained under this section shall be applicable from April 1, 2026.

G.1 Policy Aspects

323. The policy on lending against gold and silver collateral as required in terms of Reserve Bank of India (Rural Cooperative Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the policy’ in this Section) / SOPs prepared under the policy shall cover the conduct related aspects relating to:

(1) assaying procedure of jewellery, ornaments or coins made of gold or silver (“eligible collateral” for this section);

(2) criteria / qualifications for employing gold and silver assayer or valuer;

(3) auction procedure specifying, inter alia, the trigger event for the auction of eligible collateral and timeline for serving an auction notice upon the borrower;

(4) mode of auction;

(5) notice period allowed to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) for settlement of loan before auction;

(6) empanelment of auctioneers;

(7) procedure to be followed in case of loss of eligible collateral pledged or any deterioration or discrepancy in quantity or purity of eligible collateral during internal audit or otherwise, including at the time of return or auction of the collateral, and fair compensation to be paid to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) in such cases, with timelines for effecting the same, etc.

G.2 Standardisation of procedure for assaying and valuation of gold and silver collateral

324. An RCB, which provides or intends to provide loans against eligible collateral, shall ensure that a standardised procedure is put in place to assay the purity of gold and silver collateral, its weight (gross as well as net), etc. This procedure shall be adopted uniformly across all its branches for all assaying procedures.

325. An RCB shall display on its website the methodology adopted by it for determination of net weight of the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral and the price used to value the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral for determination of LTV ratio.

326. An RCB shall ensure presence of the borrower(s) while assaying the collateral at the time of sanctioning the loan. The deductions relating to stone weight, fastenings, etc., as part of the assaying procedure shall be explained to the borrower(s) and details incorporated in the certificate to be issued as per paragraph 330 below.

327. Post pledging, cases involving loss of gold or silver collateral and any deterioration or discrepancy in quantity or purity observed during internal audit or otherwise including at the time of return or auction of collateral shall be recorded and communicated promptly to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s). The process for making reimbursement or compensation as per the policy or SOP shall also be communicated to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).

G.3 Standardisation of documents and communication

328. Documentation shall be standardised across all branches of an RCB.

329. The loan agreement shall cover the description of the eligible collateral taken as security; value of such collateral; details of auction procedure and the circumstances leading to the auction of the eligible collateral; the notice period which shall be allowed to the borrower for repayment or settlement of loan before the auction is conducted; timelines for release of pledged eligible collateral upon full repayment or settlement of loan; refund of surplus, if any, from the auction of the pledged eligible collateral and other necessary details. All applicable charges payable by the borrower, including those related to assaying, auction, etc., shall be clearly included in the loan agreement and KFS.

330. An RCB, while accepting the eligible collateral, shall prepare a certificate or e-certificate in duplicate on its letterhead regarding the assay of the collateral and state therein the purity (in terms of carats); gross weight of the eligible collateral pledged; net weight of gold or silver content therein and deductions, if any, relating to weight of stones, lac, alloy, strings, fastenings, etc.; damage, breakage or defects, if any, noticed in the collateral; image of the collateral; and the value of collateral arrived at the time of sanction (as per the instructions on valuation and assaying of Gold and Silver collateral specified in the Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025) . One copy of the certificate or e-certificate shall be kept as part of the loan documents and the other copy shall be given to the borrower under her / his acknowledgement.

331. All communication with the borrower, especially, the terms and conditions of the loan, or other important communication which affects the interest of the borrower or the lender, shall be in the language of the region or in a language as chosen by the borrower. For an illiterate borrower, important terms and conditions shall be explained in the presence of a witness, who shall not be an employee of the RCB.

G.4 Handling and storage of collateral

332. An RCB shall ensure that necessary infrastructure and facilities are put in place and appropriate security measures taken in each of its branches where loans are sanctioned against gold and / or silver collateral.

333. An RCB shall ensure that the gold and / or silver collateral is handled only in its branches and only by its employees.

334. An RCB shall store the collateral only in its branches which are manned by its employees and having safe deposit vaults fit for storing gold and silver. Normally, such loans shall not be extended by branches that do not have appropriate secured facility for storage of the pledged eligible collateral.

335. The pledged eligible collateral may be transported from one branch to another branch, only as permitted under paragraph 344 below or in case of shifting or closure of branch(es) or exceptional reasons as per the process laid down by the RCB in terms of its policy.

336. An RCB shall periodically review the adequacy of systems for storage of the eligible collateral, conduct training of the concerned staff and carry out internal audit of all procedures to ensure that these are strictly adhered to.

337. As part of internal audit, an RCB shall carry out periodic surprise verification of the gold and silver collateral pledged with it and shall maintain a record thereof. A clause in the loan agreement shall be included for obtaining consent of the borrower(s) to carry out surprise verification including assay of the pledged eligible collateral even in their absence during the tenor of the loan. This aspect shall be specifically communicated to the borrower at the time of sanctioning the loan.

G.5 Release of collateral after repayment

338. An RCB shall release or return the pledged eligible collateral held as security to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) on the same day but in any case, not exceeding a maximum period of seven working days upon full repayment or settlement of the loan.

339. At the time of release of pledged eligible collateral to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s), the collateral shall be verified for correctness as per details in the certificate to the borrowers’ satisfaction.

G.6 Transparency in auction procedure

340. An RCB shall give adequate notice to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s), as applicable, through available means of communication to repay or settle the loan dues prior to initiating the auction procedure. A copy of the notice and acknowledgement thereof shall be kept on record in both scenarios. In case the lender is unable to locate the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) despite best efforts and even after issuance of a public notice, it may proceed with the auction, provided that a period of one month has lapsed from the date of the public notice.

341. An RCB shall implement a transparent auction procedure, which shall include, inter alia, announcement of the auction to the public by issue of advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and another in a national daily.

342. The pledged eligible collateral shall be auctioned by an RCB only through its employee having necessary experience and / or training or an auctioneer empanelled by the RCB as per its policy. In cases where auctions are conducted by the RCB through its employees, necessary safeguards such as surprise visits by regional / controlling officials on periodic basis, coverage under internal audit, etc., shall be put in place.

343. An RCB shall declare a reserve price for the gold and silver collateral at the time of auction, which shall not be less than 90 per cent of its current value.

Provided that in case auctions fail twice, a reserve price not less than 85 per cent of its current value shall be adopted.

344. The first auction shall be conducted physically in the same district in which the lending branch is located. However, in case of failure of first auction, an RCB may conduct the auction in an adjoining district or conduct online auction.

345. As a matter of policy, an RCB or its related parties shall not participate in the auctions to ensure that there is no potential conflict of interest.

346. After the auction, an RCB shall mandatorily provide full details of the value fetched at the auction and the dues adjusted to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s). The surplus, if any, from the auction of the gold or silver collateral, shall be refunded to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) within a maximum period of seven working days from the date of receipt of the full auction proceeds. The RCB may recover shortfall, if any, as per terms of the loan agreement.

G.7 Compensation

347. In case of any damage to the pledged eligible collateral by an RCB during the tenor of loan, the cost of repair shall be borne by the lender.

348. In case of loss of the pledged eligible collateral and / or any loss emanating from deterioration or discrepancy in quantity or purity observed during internal audit or otherwise including at the time of return or auction of collateral, an RCB shall suitably compensate the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).

349. In case of delay in release of the pledged collateral after full repayment or settlement of loan by the borrower, where reasons for delay are attributable to the RCB, it shall compensate the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay beyond the timeline prescribed at paragraph 338 above. If the delay is not attributable to the RCB, it shall communicate reasons for such delay to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s). Further, where the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) has not approached the RCB for release of pledged eligible collateral after full repayment or settlement of loan, the RCB shall issue periodic reminders to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) through letters, email or SMS if the email and mobile number are registered with the RCB.

350. The compensation provided under these directions shall be without prejudice to the rights of a borrower / legal heir to get any other compensation as per any applicable law.

G.8 Unclaimed gold and silver collateral

351. The pledged gold or silver collateral lying with an RCB beyond two years from the date of full repayment or settlement of loan shall be treated as unclaimed. The RCB shall periodically undertake special drives to ascertain the whereabouts of the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) in respect of such unclaimed gold and / or silver collateral.

352. A report on unclaimed gold and silver collateral shall be put up to the Customer Service Committee or the Board, as the case may be, at half-yearly intervals for a review.

G.9 Other Instructions

353. An RCB shall refrain from issuance of misleading advertisements containing unrealistic claims to promote loans against gold or silver collateral.

354. An RCB shall ensure that all arrangements for sourcing and/ or recovery of loans against eligible collateral, are in compliance with applicable directions on outsourcing and recovery practices issued by the Reserve Bank.

355. For prudential related aspects, the RCB shall be guided by the instructions contained in the Chapter on ‘Lending against Gold and Silver Collateral’ in Reserve Bank of India (Rural Cooperative Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 .

H. Conduct towards Microfinance Borrowers

H.1 General

356. A Fair Practices Code (FPC) based on these directions shall be put in place by an RCB with the approval of its Board. The FPC shall be displayed by the RCB in all its branches and on its website. The FPC shall be issued in a language understood by the borrower.

357. There shall be a standard form of loan agreement for microfinance loans in a language understood by the borrower.

358. An RCB shall provide a loan card to the borrower which shall incorporate the following:

(1) Information which adequately identifies the borrower;

(2) Simplified factsheet on pricing;

(3) All other terms and conditions attached to the loan;

(4) Acknowledgements by the RCB of all repayments including instalments received and the final discharge; and

(5) Details of the grievance redressal system, including the name and contact number of the nodal officer of the RCB.

359. All entries in the loan card shall be in a language understood by the borrower.

360. Issuance of non-credit products shall be with full consent of the borrowers and fee structure for such products shall be explicitly communicated to the borrower in the loan card itself.

H.2 Conduct aspects in pricing of microfinance loans

361. There shall be no pre-payment charge levied on microfinance loans. Charges, if any, for delayed payment shall be applied on the overdue amount and not on the entire loan amount.

362. An RCB shall prominently display the minimum, maximum and average interest rates charged on microfinance loans in all its offices, in the literature (information booklets/ pamphlets) issued by it and details on its website. This information shall also be included in the supervisory returns and subjected to supervisory scrutiny.

363. Any change in interest rate or any other charge shall be informed to the borrower well in advance and these changes shall be effective only prospectively.

364. As part of their awareness campaigns, Self-Regulatory Organisations (SROs) / other industry associations may publish the range of interest rates on microfinance loans charged by their members operating in a district. SROs / other industry associations may also sensitize their members against charging of usurious interest rates.

365. Reserve Bank shall also make available information regarding interest charged by RCBs on microfinance loans.

H.3 Training of Staff

366. An RCB shall have a board approved policy regarding the conduct of employees and system for their recruitment, training and monitoring. This policy shall, inter alia, lay down minimum qualifications for the staff and shall provide necessary training tools to deal with the customers. Training to employees shall include programs to inculcate appropriate behaviour towards customers. Conduct of employees towards customers shall also be incorporated appropriately in their compensation matrix.

367. Field staff shall be trained to make necessary enquiries regarding the income and existing debt of the household.

368. Training, if any, offered to the borrowers shall be free of cost.

H.4 Recovery of microfinance loans

369. An RCB shall put in place a mechanism for identification of the borrowers facing repayment related difficulties, engagement with such borrowers and providing them necessary guidance about the recourse available.

370. Recovery shall be made at a designated / central designated place decided mutually by the borrower and the RCB. However, field staff shall be allowed to make recovery at the place of residence or work of the borrower if the borrower fails to appear at the designated / central designated place on two or more successive occasions.

371. An RCB or its agent shall not engage in any harsh methods towards recovery. Without limiting the general application of the foregoing, following practices shall be deemed as harsh:

(1) Use of threatening or abusive language

(2) Persistently calling the borrower and / or calling the borrower before 9:00 a.m. and after 6:00 p.m.

(3) Harassing relatives, friends, or co-workers of the borrower

(4) Publishing the names of borrowers

(5) Use or threat of use of violence or other similar means to harm the borrower or borrower’s family / assets / reputation

(6) Misleading the borrower about the extent of the debt or the consequences of non-repayment.

372.An RCB shall have a dedicated mechanism for redressal of recovery related grievances. The details of this mechanism shall be provided to the borrower at the time of loan disbursal.

H.5 Engagement of recovery agents for recovery of microfinance loans

373. Recovery agents shall mean agencies engaged by an RCB for recovery of dues from its borrowers and the employees of these agencies.

374. An RCB shall have a due diligence process in place for engagement of recovery agents, which shall, inter alia, cover individuals involved in the recovery process. The RCB shall ensure that the recovery agents engaged by them carry out verification of the antecedents of its employees, which shall include police verification. The RCB shall also decide the periodicity at which re-verification of antecedents shall be resorted to.

375. To ensure due notice and appropriate authorisation, an RCB shall provide the details of recovery agents to the borrower while initiating the process of recovery. The agent shall also carry a copy of the notice and the authorisation letter from the RCB along with the identity card issued to her / him by the RCB or the agency. Further, where the recovery agency is changed by the RCB during the recovery process, in addition to the RCB notifying the borrower of the change, the new agent shall carry the notice and the authorisation letter along with her / his identity card.

376. The notice and the authorisation letter shall, among other details, also include the contact details of the recovery agency and the RCB.

377. The up-to-date details of the recovery agencies engaged by an RCB shall also be hosted on the RCB’s website.

I. Responsibilities of RCBs employing recovery agents

378. An RCB shall strictly ensure that it or its agents do not resort to intimidation or harassment of any kind, either verbal or physical, against any person in their debt collection efforts, including acts intended to humiliate publicly or intrude upon the privacy of the debtors' family members, referees and friends, sending inappropriate messages either on mobile or through social media, making threatening and / or anonymous calls, persistently calling the borrower and/ or calling the borrower before 8:00 a.m. and after 7:00 p.m. for recovery of overdue loans, making false and misleading representations, etc. These directions shall not be applicable to microfinance loans.

Chapter IX – Miscellaneous

A. Accepting standing instructions of customers

379. Standing instructions shall be freely accepted on all current and savings bank accounts. The scope of standing instructions service shall be expanded to include payments on account of taxes, rents, bills, school / college fees, licences, etc.

B. Clean overdrafts for small amounts

380. Clean overdrafts for small amounts may be permitted at the discretion of branch manager to customers whose dealings have been satisfactory. An RCB may work out schemes in this regard.

C. Rounding off of transactions

381. All transactions, including payment of interest on deposits / charging of interest on advances, should be rounded off to the nearest rupee i.e., fractions of 50 paise and above shall be rounded off to the next higher rupee and fraction of less than 50 paise shall be ignored.

382. Issue prices of cash certificates should also be rounded off in the same manner. However, an RCB shall ensure that cheques / drafts issued by clients containing fractions of a rupee are not rejected or dishonoured by it. The RCB shall ensure that appropriate action is taken against members of its staff who are found to have refused to accept cheques / drafts containing fractions of a rupee.

D. Declaration of Holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881

383. In terms of Section 25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, the expression "public holiday" includes Sunday and any other day declared by the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette to be a public holiday. However, this power has been delegated by the Central Government to State Governments vide the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs' Notification No. 20-25-56-Pub-I dated June 8, 1957. While delegating the power to declare public holidays within concerned States under Section 25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, the Central Government has stipulated that the delegation is subject to the condition that the Central Government may itself exercise the said function, should it deem fit to do so. This implies that when Central Government itself has notified a day as "public holiday" under Section 25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, there is no need for the RCB to wait for the state government notification.

E. Co-ordination with officers of Central Board of Direct Taxes

384. An RCB shall extend necessary help / co-ordination to tax officials whenever required. Further, the RCB shall treat with utmost seriousness cases where its staff connive / assist in any manner with offences punishable under the Income Tax Act. In such cases, in addition to the normal criminal action, such staff member shall also be proceeded against departmentally.

Chapter X – Repeal and Other Provisions

A. Repeal and Savings

385. With the issue of these Directions, the existing Directions, instructions, and guidelines relating to Responsible Business Conduct as applicable to Rural Co-operative Banks stand repealed, as communicated vide circular DOR.RRC.REC.302/33-01-010/2025-26 dated November 28, 2025 . The Directions, instructions, and guidelines repealed prior to the issuance of these Directions shall continue to remain repealed.

386. Notwithstanding such repeal, any action taken or purported to have been taken, or initiated under the repealed Directions, instructions, or guidelines shall continue to be governed by the provisions thereof. All approvals or acknowledgments granted under these repealed lists shall be deemed as governed by these Directions. Further, the repeal of these directions, instructions, or guidelines shall not in any way prejudicially affect:

(1) any right, obligation or liability acquired, accrued, or incurred thereunder;

(2) any, penalty, forfeiture, or punishment incurred in respect of any contravention committed thereunder;

(3) any investigation, legal proceeding, or remedy in respect of any such right, privilege, obligation, liability, penalty, forfeiture, or punishment as aforesaid; and any such investigation, legal proceedings or remedy may be instituted, continued, or enforced and any such penalty, forfeiture or punishment may be imposed as if those directions, instructions, or guidelines had not been repealed.

B. Application of other laws not barred

387. The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

C. Interpretations

388. For the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of these Directions or in order to remove any difficulties in the application or interpretation of the provisions of these Directions, the Reserve Bank may, if it considers necessary, issue necessary clarifications in respect of any matter covered herein and the interpretation of any provision of these Directions given by the Reserve Bank shall be final and binding.

(Veena Srivastava)
Chief General Manager

4. In these Directions, unless the context states otherwise, the terms here must bear the meaning assigned to them below: (1) Accounts with survivorship clause mean joint deposit accounts styled as ‘either or survivor’, or ‘anyone or survivor’, or ‘former or survivor’ or ‘latter or survivor’ or any other such clause.
The number must be such that the account holder or the RCB branch where account is maintained, can't be identified by any third party.
5. An RCB must put in place approved policies and review mechanisms to ensure sound business conduct and enhanced customer service.
8. Matters relating to customer service must be deliberated by the Board to ensure that the instructions are implemented meaningfully.
Commitment to hassle-free service to the customer at large and the common person in particular must be the major responsibility of the Board.
9. Customer service must be projected as a priority objective of banks along with profit, growth and fulfilment of social obligations.
An RCB must have a Board approved policy for the following: B.2.1 Deposit Policy.
10. An RCB must formulate a transparent and comprehensive policy setting out the rights of the depositors in general and small depositors in particular.
The policy must cover all aspects of operations of deposit accounts, charges leviable and other related issues to facilitate interaction of depositors at branch levels.
Such a policy must also be explicit regarding secrecy and confidentiality of customers.

11. An RCB must formulate a comprehensive and transparent policy taking into account its technological capabilities, systems and processes adopted for clearing arrangements and other internal arrangements for collection through correspondents.
The policy, among other things, must cover the following three aspects: (1) Immediate credit for local / outstation cheques.

12. An RCB must have a Board approved Customer Compensation Policy which must at a minimum, incorporate the following aspects: (1) Erroneous debits arising on fraudulent or other transactions, (2) Payment of interest for delays in collection, (3) Payment of interest for delay in issue of duplicate draft, and.
13. An RCB must ensure that wide publicity is given to the above policies formulated by it by placing them prominently on the website as well as displaying them on the notice board of its branches.
The RCB must also take necessary steps to keep the customers duly informed of the changes in the policies formulated by it when needed.
The customers must be clearly apprised of the assurances of the RCB on the services provided, at the time of establishment of the initial relationship, be it as a depositor, borrower or otherwise.

14. An RCB must constitute a Customer Service Committee of the Board and include experts and representatives of customers as invitees to enable the RCB to formulate policies and assess the compliance of it internally.
15. Customer Service Committee of the Board, illustratively, must address the following: (1) Formulation of a comprehensive Deposit policy.
16. The Committee must also examine any other issues having a bearing on the quality of customer service rendered.
17. A detailed memorandum reviewing customer service / customer care aspects of an RCB must be placed once in every six months to the Board of Directors.
Prompt corrective action must be initiated wherever service quality / skill gaps are noticed.

18. An RCB must have a Standing Committee on Customer Service, cutting across various departments, which must serve as the micro level executive committee driving the implementation process and providing relevant feedback.
The Customer Service Committee of the Board must oversee and review / modify the initiatives.
These two Committees must be mutually reinforcing, with one feeding into the other.

19. The constitution and functions of the Standing Committee must be on the lines indicated below: (1) The Standing Committee must be chaired by the Chairman or MD or CEO and include non-officials as its members to enable an independent feedback on the quality of customer service rendered by the RCB.

(2) The Standing Committee must be entrusted not only with the task of ensuring timely and effective compliance of the Reserve Bank’s instructions on customer service, but also that of receiving the necessary feedback to determine that the actions taken by various departments of the RCB are in tune with the spirit and intent of such instructions.
(3) The Standing Committee must, on an ongoing basis, review the practices and procedures prevalent in the RCB and take necessary corrective action.

(4) The Standing Committee must submit a brief report periodically to the Customer Service Committee of the Board on its performance during its tenure indicating, among other things, the areas reviewed, procedures / practices identified and simplified / introduced.
(5) The Standing Committee must act as the bridge between the various departments of the RCB and the Board / Customer Service Committee of the Board.
20. An RCB must establish Customer Service Committees at branch level, which must also include its customers.
Senior citizens, an important constituent in banks, must be included in it.

21. The Branch Level Customer Service Committee must meet at least once a month to study complaints/ suggestions, cases of delay, difficulties faced / reported by customers / members of the Committee, and evolve ways and means of improving customer service.

22. The Branch Level Committees must submit quarterly reports giving inputs / suggestions to the Standing Committee on Customer Service, thus enabling the Standing Committee to examine them and provide relevant feedback to the Customer Service Committee of the Board for necessary policy / procedural action.
23. An RCB must orient its systems and procedures towards providing better customer service and must periodically assess these systems and their impact on customer service.

An RCB must have a Board approved policy for general management of the branches, which must include the following aspects: (1) Providing infrastructure facilities at branches by bestowing particular attention to providing adequate space, proper furniture, drinking water facilities, with specific emphasis on pensioners, senior citizens, disabled persons, etc. (2) Providing entirely separate enquiry counters at large / bigger branches in addition to a regular reception counter.
Business posters at semi-urban and rural branches of the RCB must also be in the concerned regional languages.
(15) Clearly establishing a new product and services approval process which must require approval by the Board, especially on issues which compromise the rights of the common person.
24. An RCB must normally function for public transactions at least for four hours on weekdays and two hours on Saturdays in the larger interest of public and trading community.
26. An RCB must give sufficient notice to the public / its customers of its intention of closing any of its branches / offices on a day other than a public holiday.
An RCB must ensure that it avoids any infringement of any other relevant local laws such as Shops and Establishments Act, etc. 27.
The provisions, if any, regarding an RCB’s obligations to its staff under Industrial Awards / Settlements, must be complied with.
Clearing House authority of the place must also be consulted in this regard.
28. An RCB must keep rural branches open on weekly market day.
The RCB must have the flexibility to fix the business hours (i.e.
This must, however, be done subject to the instructions given above.

30. An RCB must devise appropriate procedures to ensure that no counter remains unattended during the business hours and uninterrupted service is rendered to the customers by making adequate relief arrangements as may be necessary.
31. An RCB must extend business hours for banking transactions other than cash, up to one hour before the close of working hours.
33. Further, the non-cash transactions to be done during the extended business hours must be notified adequately for information of the customers.

35. An RCB must give to its constituents due notice about the functions to be undertaken during the extended working hours, through local newspapers, as also by displaying a notice on the Notice Board at the branch(es) concerned.
It must also be ensured that the requirements of Shops and Establishments Act.
37. An RCB must make available to the customers brochures / pamphlets in regional language / Hindi / English giving details of various schemes available and terms and conditions of it.

A customer must be made aware not only of the various schemes and services offered by an RCB, but also about the formalities, procedures, legal requirements and limitations in the matter of providing services by the RCB, through a proper mix of advertisements, literature, interface, seminars, etc. The RCB must involve its employees in all customer education programmes.
39. An RCB must keep its systems and procedures in trim, by a continuous process of introduction of new procedures that may be required and by doing away with unwanted ones.
41. Instructions of a customer for transfer of her / his account to another branch must be carried out immediately on receipt of, and as per, her / his instructions.

It must be ensured that along with the balance of the account, the account opening form, specimen signatures, standing instructions, etc. or the master sheets wherever obtained, are also simultaneously transferred, under an advice to the customer.
42. The account transfer form with the enclosures must be handed over to the customer in a sealed cover if she / he so desires for delivery at the transferee branch.
However, the transferee branch must also be separately supplied with a copy of the account transfer letter.

43. When a branch receives an enquiry from a customer regarding the receipt of her / his account on transfer from another branch, it must take up the matter with the transferor branch by electronic means in case it has not received the balance of the account and / or other related papers even after a reasonable transit time.
44. An RCB must ensure that depositors dissatisfied with customer service have the facility to switch banks.
Thwarting depositors from such switches must invite adverse action.

45. An RCB must have “Enquiry” or “May I Help You” counters either exclusively or combined with other duties, located near the entry point of the banking hall, at all branches (excluding very small branches).
46. An RCB must display the time norms for specialised business transactions predominantly in the banking hall.
47. An RCB must adhere to the following instructions on display of information.
An RCB must have a comprehensive notice board to display information at its branches as per the format given in Annex I.

49. While displaying the information on the notice board, an RCB must adhere to the following principles: (1) The notice board must be updated on a periodical basis, which must indicate the date up to which it has been updated.
(2) Though the RCB must have discretion on pattern, colour and design of the board, the display must be kept simple and readable.
(3) The notice board must be bilingual in Hindi speaking states and trilingual in other states.
(4) The notice board must specifically indicate where recent changes have been made.
(5) The notice board must also indicate a list of items on which detailed information is available in booklet form.
50. In addition to the above board, an RCB must also display details such as ‘Name of the RCB / branch, Working Days, Working Hours and Weekly Off-days' outside the branch premises.
(3) While printing the booklets, it must be ensured while printing the booklets that the font size is a minimum of Arial 10 so that the customers are able to easily read them.
52. An RCB must make available the detailed information indicated in Paragraph (D) of Annex I on its website.
It must be ensured that the customers are able to easily access the relevant information from the Home Page of the RCB’s website.
The RCB must adhere to the broad guidelines relating to dating of material, legibility, etc. while placing the same on its websites.
53. An RCB must display latest updated information relating to interest rates and service charges as per the format given in Annex II on its website.
The same must be easily accessible from the Home Page of its website.

55. to ensure that banking facilities percolate to the vast sections of the population, an RCB must make available all printed material used by retail customers including account opening forms, pay-in-slips, passbooks, etc. in trilingual form i.e.

56. An RCB must adhere to the instructions and procedures for opening and operating deposit accounts to safeguard against unscrupulous persons opening accounts mainly to use them as conduit for fraudulently encashing payment instruments.

However, in view of receipt of continuous complaints of fraudulent encashment by unscrupulous persons opening deposit accounts in the name(s) similar to already established entities, resulting in erroneous and unauthorised debit of drawers’ accounts, an RCB must remain vigilant to prevent such lapses and issue necessary instructions to its branches / staff.

Therefore, an RCB is advised that: (1) in case of any fraud, if the branch is convinced that an irregularity / fraud has been committed by its staff towards any constituent, the branch must at once acknowledge its liability and pay the just claim, (2) in cases where the RCB is at fault, it must compensate customers without demur, and.

(3) in cases where neither the RCB nor the customer is at fault but the fault lies elsewhere in the system, then also the RCB must compensate the customers (up to a limit) as part of its Board approved customer relations policy.
59. The systems and procedures in RCBs must be designed to make customers feel safe about carrying out electronic banking transactions.
To achieve this, an RCB must put in place: (1) appropriate systems and procedures to ensure safety and security of electronic banking transactions carried out by customers.
60. An RCB must ask its customers to mandatorily register for SMS alerts and wherever available, register for e-mail alerts, for electronic banking transactions.
The SMS alerts must mandatorily be sent to the customers, while email alerts may be sent, wherever registered.

The customers must be advised to notify their bank of any unauthorised electronic banking transaction at the earliest after the occurrence of such transaction and informed that the longer the time taken to notify the RCB, the higher will be the risk of loss to the RCB / customer.

To facilitate this, the RCB must provide its customers with 24x7 access through multiple channels (at a minimum, via website, phone banking, SMS, e-mail, IVR, a dedicated toll-free helpline, reporting to home branch, etc.) for reporting unauthorised transactions that have taken place and / or loss or theft of payment instrument such as card, etc. The RCB must also enable customers to instantly respond by "Reply" to the SMS and e-mail alerts.
As an alternative, the RCB must provide an alternate number in the transaction alert SMS itself, to which the customer can immediately send a reply.
Further, a direct link for lodging the complaints, with specific option to report unauthorised electronic transactions must be provided by RCBs on home page of their website.
The loss / fraud reporting system must also ensure that immediate response (including auto response) is sent to the customers acknowledging the complaint along with the registered complaint number.
The communication systems used by banks to send alerts and receive their responses to it must record the time and date of delivery of the message and receipt of customer’s response, if any, to them.
This must be important in determining the extent of a customer’s liability.
The RCB must not offer facility of electronic transactions, other than ATM cash withdrawals, to customers who don't provide mobile numbers to it.
On receipt of report of an unauthorised transaction from the customer, the RCB must take immediate steps to prevent further unauthorised transactions in the account.

61. A customer’s entitlement to zero liability must arise where the unauthorised transaction occurs in the following events: (1) Contributory fraud / negligence / deficiency on the part of the RCB (irrespective of whether the transaction is reported by the customer or not).

62. A customer must be liable for the loss occurring due to unauthorised transactions in the following cases: (1) In cases where the loss is due to negligence by a customer, such as where she / he has shared the payment credentials, the customer will bear the entire loss until she / he reports the unauthorised transaction to the RCB.
Any loss occurring after the reporting of the unauthorised transaction must be borne by the RCB.

(2) In cases where the responsibility for the unauthorised electronic banking transaction lies neither with the RCB nor with the customer, but lies elsewhere in the system and the customer notifies the RCB of such a transaction within four to seven working days of receiving a communication of the transaction, the per transaction liability of the customer must be limited to the transaction value or the amount mentioned in Table 1, whichever is lower.
63. Further, if the delay in reporting is beyond seven working days, the customer liability must be determined as per the RCB’s Board approved policy.
The RCB must provide the details of its policy regarding customers’ liability formulated in pursuance of these directions at the time of opening the accounts.
The RCB must also display its approved policy in public domain for wider dissemination.
The existing customers must also be individually informed about the RCB’s policy.
65. The number of working days mentioned in Table 2 must be counted as per the working schedule of the home branch of the customer excluding the date of receiving the communication.

66. On being notified by the customer, an RCB must credit (shadow reversal) the amount involved in the unauthorised electronic transaction to the customer’s account within 10 working days from the date of such notification by the customer (without waiting for settlement of insurance claim, if any).
The credit must be value dated to be as of the date of the unauthorised transaction.
The credit must be value dated to be as of the date of the unauthorised transaction.
67. Further, an RCB must ensure that: (1) a complaint is resolved and liability of the customer, if any, established.

68. An RCB must formulate / revise their customer relations policy with approval of their Boards, which must clearly define the rights and obligations of customers in case of unauthorized transactions in specified scenarios, i.e.

Debits to customer accounts owning to customer negligence / bank negligence / banking system frauds / third party breaches, etc. The policy must also include mechanism of creating customer awareness on the risks and responsibilities involved in electronic banking transactions, and customer liability in case of unauthorized electronic banking transactions, procedure for reporting unauthorized electronic banking transactions and acknowledgement of complaints.
The instructions contained in this section must be incorporated in the policy, and the policy must be prominently displayed at branches.
69. The burden of proving customer liability in case of unauthorised electronic banking transactions must lie on the RCB.
70. An RCB must put in place a suitable mechanism and structure for the reporting of the customer liability cases to the Board or one of its Committees.
The reporting must, among other things, include volume / number of cases and the aggregate value involved and distribution across various categories of cases viz.

Card present transactions, card not present transactions, internet banking, mobile banking, ATM transactions, etc. The Board must periodically review the unauthorised electronic banking transactions reported by customers or otherwise, as also the action taken thereon, the functioning of the grievance redress mechanism and take appropriate measures to improve the systems and procedures.
All such transactions must be reviewed by the RCB’s internal auditors.
71. An RCB must work out the service charges for various types of services like charges for cheque collection etc. with prior approval of its Board of Directors.
These charges must be reasonable and not out of line with the average cost of providing these services.
The RCB must also take care to ensure that customers with low volume of activities aren't penalised.
72. An RCB must adopt / follow the principles outlined below for ensuring reasonableness in fixing and communicating service charges.
73. Identification of basic banking services: An RCB must identify basic banking services based on the following broad parameters: (1) Nature of transactions.
(a) Banking services that are ordinarily availed by individuals in the middle and lower segments must be the first parameter.
(a) Low value transactions with customers / public up to the ceiling as given below must be the second parameter: - Remittances up to ₹10,000 in each instance.

74. Offering basic banking services outside the scope of bundled products: An RCB must make available the basic banking services at reasonable prices / charges and towards this, basic services must be delivered outside the scope of bundled products.

75. Principles for ensuring reasonableness in fixing and communicating service charges: (1) For basic services to individuals, an RCB must levy charges at the rates that are lower than the rates applied when the same services are given to non-individuals.

(2) For basic services rendered to special category of individuals (such as individuals in rural areas, pensioners and senior citizens), an RCB must levy charges on more liberal terms than the terms on which the charges are levied to other individuals.
(3) For the basic services rendered to individuals, an RCB must levy charges only if the charges are just and supported by reason.
(4) For the basic services to individuals, an RCB must levy services charges ad-valorem only to cover any incremental cost and subject to a cap.
(5) An RCB must provide to individual customers upfront and in a timely manner, complete information on the charges applicable to all basic services.
(6) An RCB must provide advance information to individual customers about the proposed changes in service charges.
(7) An RCB must collect for services given to individuals only such charges which have been notified to the customer.
(8) An RCB must inform its customers in an appropriate manner about recovery of service charges from the account or the transaction.

(9) An RCB must, without fail, inform its customers in all cases when a transaction initiated by the RCB itself results in or is likely to lead to a shortfall in the minimum balance required to be maintained.

The following instructions must be followed in this regard: (1) Disclosure of service charges: (i) An RCB must communicate service charges to new customers at the time of beginning of the relationship.

(ii) Service charges must be displayed in the notice board at the branch so as to disseminate information to customers / public, in addition to display on the website, as per extant instructions of the Reserve Bank.
(iii) The RCB must also put in place appropriate methods for communicating service charges to customers of different profiles.

(2) Notifying the changes effected in service charges: (i) An RCB must take steps to ensure that any change in the service charges is effected only with prior notification to customers of at least 30 days.
(ii) The RCB must provide an option to customers to accept the change.
(iv) The RCB must prominently display in the notice board as well as the website all the changes in service charges effected in the preceding 30 days.

77. Financial education: An RCB must disclose full-fledged information on its products and their implications to the customers so that the customers can make an informed judgment about their choice of products.
78. An RCB must follow a uniform, fair and transparent pricing policy and not discriminate between its customers at home branch and non-home branches.
A service provided free at home branch must be available free at non-home branches also.

There must be no discrimination as regards intersol charges (being the charges levied by an RCB to cover the cost of extending services to customers by using the CBS / Internet / Intranet platform) between similar transactions done by customers at home branch and those done at non-home branches.
Further, an RCB must not include cash handling charges under intersol charges.
79. An RCB must leverage the technology available with it.
Every RCB must offer a BSBD account which must be considered a normal banking service available to all.
An RCB must offer the following basic minimum facilities in a BSBD account, free of charge, without any requirement of minimum balance to be maintained in such an account.
Further, no charges must be levied towards annual fee, either at the time of issuance or renewal.
Further, issuance of a continuation passbook, on exhaustion of the pages in the previous passbook, must not attract any charge.
Point of Sale transfers, NEFT, RTGS, UPI, IMPS, etc. must not be counted as withdrawals for this purpose.

The charges on digital payment transactions must be as per guidelines issued by Department of Payment and Settlement Systems, Reserve Bank / National Payments Corporation of India / Government of India,.

80A. The facilities of ATM / ATM-cum-Debit card or internet / mobile banking or cheque book must be offered to a customer provided she / he requests for the same, whether at the time of opening the account or subsequently.
An RCB must not insist that a customer necessarily avails these facilities while opening and / or operating the BSBD account.
81. In the case of existing BSBD accounts, an RCB must extend the newly introduced free facilities at clause (5) to (7) of paragraph 80 above upon receipt of a request from the customer.
The RCB must facilitate existing BSBD account holders to submit such requests through physical as well as digital channels.
However, while doing so, the RCB must not require the customer to maintain a minimum balance in the BSBD account.
The availment of such additional facilities must be at the option of the customer.

83. Opening and operation of BSBD accounts must be subject to the instructions on Know Your Customer / Anti Money Laundering issued by the Reserve Bank through ‘Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks – Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025 ’, as amended when needed.
Further, BSBD accounts opened by or operated on behalf of minors must be subject to the instructions contained in paragraphs 166 to 171 below of these Directions.
84. An RCB, while opening a BSBD account, must not impose any requirement of an initial minimum deposit.
The RCB must convert the existing savings bank account to a BSBD account within seven days of receipt of request in writing from the customer for such conversion.
Such an option must also be provided to customers through digital channels.
86. The holder of a BSBD account must not be eligible to open another BSBD account in the same RCB or any other bank.

Accordingly, before opening a new BSBD account or converting an existing savings bank account to a BSBD account, the RCB must obtain a declaration from the customer that she / he doesn't have a BSBD account in any other bank.
87. An RCB must publicise the availability of a BSBD account and its features to customers.
The RCB must also convey the differences between a BSBD account and various savings bank account variants offered by it when a customer approaches it to open a deposit account.
88. An RCB must take necessary steps to provide all its ATMs with ramps so that Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) / wheelchair users can easily access them.
Care must also be taken to make arrangements in such a way that the height of the ATMs doesn't create an impediment in their use by wheelchair users.
89. An RCB must also take appropriate steps, including providing ramps at the entrance of the branches, wherever feasible.
An RCB must report the progress made in this regard periodically to their respective Customer Service Committee of the Board and ensure compliance.

90. An RCB must ensure that all the banking facilities such as cheque book facility including third party cheques, ATM facility, internet banking facility, locker facility, retail loans, credit cards etc. are invariably offered to the visually impaired without any discrimination.
They must also be assisted in withdrawal of cash.
91. An RCB must also advise its branches to render all possible assistance to the visually impaired for availing various banking facilities.
92. An RCB must ensure that all its ATMs are Talking ATMs equipped with Braille keypads.
93. Magnifying glasses must also be provided in all bank branches for the use of persons with low vision, wherever they require for carrying out banking transactions with ease.
The branches must display at a prominent place notice about the availability of magnifying glasses and other facilities available for PwDs.
94. An RCB must extend the following facilities to account holders who are old/ sick/ incapacitated and who aren't willing to open and operate joint accounts.

96. With a view to enabling the old / sick / incapacitated account holders to operate their bank accounts, an RCB must follow the procedure as under: (1) Wherever thumb or toe impression of the old / sick / incapacitated account holder is obtained, it must be identified by two independent witnesses known to the RCB, one of whom must be a responsible official of the RCB.

(2) Where the customer can't even put her / his thumb impression and is also unable to be physically present in the RCB, a mark can be obtained on the cheque / withdrawal form which must be identified by two independent witnesses, one of whom must be a responsible official of the RCB.
(3) The customer must also be asked to indicate to the RCB as to who would withdraw the amount from the RCB on the basis of cheque / withdrawal form as obtained above.
The person who would be actually drawing the money from the RCB must be asked to furnish her / his signature to the RCB.

97. In case of attachment and recovery of the contents in a locker of a customer or the articles left by a customer for safe custody of an RCB by any authority acting either under the orders of a court or any other competent authority vested with the power to pass such orders, the RCB must co-operate in execution and implementation of the orders.
227. An RCB must verify and satisfy itself about the orders and the connected documents received for attachment and recovery of the contents in a locker or articles in the safe custody of the RCB.

The customer (locker-hirer) must be informed by letter as well as by email / SMS to the registered email address / mobile phone number that the government authorities have approached for attachment and recovery or seizure of the locker or articles deposited for safe custody.
An inventory of the contents of locker and articles seized and recovered by the authority must be prepared in the presence of such government authorities, two independent witnesses.

228. An RCB must also record a video of the break-open process and the inventory assessment, wherever legally permissible, and preserve the video to produce as evidence in case of any dispute or court case or fraud case in future.
229. An RCB must have the discretion to break open any locker following due procedure if the rent has not been paid by the customer for three years in a row.
The RCB must ensure to notify the existing locker-hirer before any changes in the allotment and give her / him reasonable opportunity to withdraw the articles deposited by her / him.
230. Before breaking open the locker, an RCB must give due notice to the locker-hirer through a letter and through email and SMS alert to the registered email address and mobile phone number.
If the letter is returned undelivered or the locker-hirer isn't traceable, the RCB must issue public notice in two newspaper dailies (one in English.
231. The locker must be broken open in the presence of an officer of the RCB and two independent witnesses.

In case of electronically operated lockers (including smart vaults), the use of ‘Vault Administrator’ password for opening of locker must be assigned to a senior official and complete audit trail of access must be preserved.

Further, the RCB must also record a video of the break open process together with inventory assessment and its safekeep and preserve the same so as to provide evidence in case of any dispute or court case in future.

The RCB must also ensure that the details of breaking open of locker is documented in CBS or any other computerised systems compliant with the cyber security framework issued by Reserve Bank, apart from locker register.
232. After breaking open of locker, the contents must be kept in sealed envelope with detailed inventory inside fireproof safe in a tamper-proof way until the customer claims it.
A record of access to the fireproof safe must invariably be maintained.
While returning the contents of the locker, an RCB must obtain acknowledgement of the customer on the inventory list to avoid any dispute in future.
233. An RCB must ensure that the inventory prepared after breaking open of the locker is as per [***] 3 Annex X or as near to it as circumstances require.

Further, an RCB must not open sealed / closed packets left with them for safe custody or found in locker while releasing them to the nominee(s) and surviving locker hirers / depositor of safe custody article, unless required by law.

234. If the locker remains inoperative for a period of seven years and the locker-hirer can't be located, even if rent is being paid regularly, an RCB must be at liberty to transfer the contents of the locker to nominee(s) / legal heir(s) of the locker-hirer or dispose of the articles in a transparent manner,.
Before breaking open the locker, the RCB must follow the procedure as prescribed in paragraphs 230 to 233 above.

The RCB must ensure that the procedure to be followed by it for disposal of the articles left unclaimed for a reasonably long period of time as mentioned above is incorporated in its locker agreement.
235. An RCB must ensure that appropriate terms are inserted in the locker agreement executed with the customer specifying the position in case the locker isn't in operation for long period.

236. An RCB must put in place a detailed Board approved policy outlining the responsibility owed by them for any loss or damage to the contents of the lockers due to its negligence as RCBs owe a separate duty of care to exercise due diligence in maintaining and operating its locker or safety deposit systems.

Further, the RCB must adhere to the Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks – Fraud Risk Management) Directions, 2026, as amended when needed, for reporting requirements about the instances of robberies, dacoities, thefts and burglaries.

As the RCB can't claim that they bear no liability towards its customers for loss of contents of the locker, in instances where loss of contents of locker is due to incidents mentioned above or attributable to fraud committed by its employee(s), the RCB’s liability must be for an amount equivalent to one hundred times the prevailing annual rent of the safe deposit locker.

239. An RCB, with the approval of its Board, must have a branch insurance policy to minimize the loss due to incidents like robbery, fire, natural calamities, loss during shifting / merger of branch, etc. affecting contents of lockers.

240. An RCB must clarify in its locker agreement that as it doesn't keep a record of the contents of the locker or of any articles removed therefrom or placed in it by the customer, they would not be under any liability to insure the contents of the locker against any risk whatsoever.
The RCB must under no circumstances offer, directly or indirectly, any insurance product to its locker hirers for insurance of locker contents.
241. An RCB must display the model locker agreement with all the terms & conditions.
The RCB must ensure that the customers are made aware of its terms and conditions to avail those facilities.
242. An RCB must display updated information on all kinds of charges for safe deposit lockers and safe custody articles on its website.

243. An RCB must place on its website, the instructions together with the policies / procedures put in place for giving access of the locker / safe custody article to the nominee(s) / survivor(s) / legal heir(s) of the deceased locker hirer / safe custody article.
Further, a printed copy of the same must also be given to the nominee(s) / survivor(s) / legal heir(s).

Accordingly, these Directions are issued to banks to implement the nomination facility and must be read with sections 45ZA to 45ZG and section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and the Nomination Rules framed thereunder.
These Directions must be applicable from November 1, 2025.
245. An RCB must offer nomination facility in deposit accounts under sections 45ZA, 45ZB and 45ZG of the Act (read with section 56 of the Act) and the Rules.

246. An RCB must be guided by the rules in sections 45ZC to 45ZG of the Act (read with section 56 of the Act) and the Rules in the matter of nomination in safe deposit lockers and articles kept in safe custody.
Explanation: For the purpose of these Directions, it's clarified that if an individual is maintaining an account for her / his proprietorship business, it will be deemed as that individual’s account.

247. At the time of account opening, an RCB must explicitly inform the prospective customer of the availability and purpose of the nomination facility and offer her / him the option to avail the same.

The RCB must also clearly explain to the prospective customer the advantages of the nomination facility, including simplification of the claim process if the account holder’s demise and facilitation of smooth and prompt transfer of funds to the nominee without legal complications.

248. If the prospective customer chooses not to avail the nomination facility despite being fully informed, the RCB must proceed to open the deposit account without imposing any restrictions, if otherwise found eligible, after obtaining a written declaration from the individual confirming that she / he doesn't require the nomination facility at the time of account opening.
If she / he refuses to provide the written declaration, the RCB must record the fact of refusal to submit written confirmation in the account opening records.

249. Under no circumstances must a prospective customer be denied or delayed in opening an account solely on the ground of refusal to make a nomination, provided all other requirements for account opening are satisfactorily met.
250. In case of simultaneous nomination, if any nominee dies before receiving the deposit from an RCB, the nomination in respect of such nominee alone must become ineffective.

Accordingly, an RCB must settle the claims of the amount of deposit made in favour of such nominee as per provisions applicable for accounts without nominee clause as contained in paragraphs 267 to 274 of these Directions.
252. An RCB must have in place appropriate systems and procedures to register in its books the registration, cancellation and variation of the nomination, as per the request of the customers.
253. An RCB must devise proper systems for acknowledging the receipt of the duly completed forms of registration, cancellation and / or variation of the nomination.
254. An RCB must verify and ensure that the nomination(s) made by its customers are as per relevant provisions of the Act and the Rules before providing acknowledgement to them.

255. Such acknowledgement must be given to the customers within three working days of receiving the forms of registration, cancellation and / or variation of nomination, irrespective of whether the same is asked for by the customers.

256. Where a nomination request is found not to be in conformity with the rules in the Act or the Rules and is consequently rejected, an RCB must inform the customer in writing, clearly indicating the reasons for such rejection, within three working days of the receipt of the request form.
257. An RCB must record the status regarding registration of nomination on the face of the passbook / statement of account and TDR, with the legend "Nomination Registered".
258. The RCB must also indicate the name of the nominee(s) in the passbook/ statement of accounts and TDR in such cases.
259. An RCB must give wide publicity and provide guidance to deposit account holders, locker hirers and depositors of articles in safe custody on the benefits of the nomination facility.

260. An RCB must ensure that the form for opening deposit accounts, hiring safe deposit lockers and depositing articles in safe custody contains a space for getting the details of nomination, which also serves the purpose of educating the customers about availability of such facility.
262. The Directions given in this section must be applicable from April 1, 2026.

These Directions must not be applicable in case of Government savings schemes administered by banks such as Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS), Public Provident Fund (PPF), etc. Settlement of claims in such cases must be as per the rules in the respective schemes.

281. In case the locker was hired jointly with survivorship clause.

283. The following documents must be obtained by a bank for processing the claim in cases falling under paragraphs 279 and 280 above: (1) Claim form, as given in Annex V, duly signed by the nominee(s)/ survivor(s).

An RCB must, however, ensure the following before giving access to the contents to the nominee(s)/ survivor(s): (1) Exercise due care and caution in establishing the identity of the nominee(s)/ survivor(s) and deceased status of the locker hirer(s) by obtaining appropriate documentary evidence (physical or equivalent e-document).
Such access and liberty to remove the contents given to them must not affect the right or claim which any person may have against the nominee(s)/ survivor(s) to whom the access is given.

Succession Certificate, Letter of Administration, Probate of Will, etc. or Bond of indemnity from the nominee(s)/ survivor(s) must not be required unless there is any discrepancy in nomination.
287. Procedure, as prescribed in paragraphs 279 to 286 above, must be followed mutatis mutandis for return of articles kept by the deceased customer in the safe custody of an RCB.
However, inventory form given in Annex XI must be used in such cases.

288. Keeping in view the imperative need to avoid inconvenience and undue hardship to the legal heir(s)/ claimant(s), a bank must adopt a simplified procedure for settlement of claims in safe deposit lockers provided there is no dispute amongst the legal heir(s)/ claimant(s) and.

289. In cases falling under the simplified procedure, an RCB must obtain the following documents to settle the claim without obtaining any legal documents such as Succession Certificate, Letter of Administration, court order, etc. (1) Claim form, as given in Annex VI, duly filled and signed by the claimant legal heir(s).

290. An RCB must settle claims involving ‘Will’ left behind by a deceased safe deposit locker hirer on the basis of Probate of Will/ Letter of Administration, in addition to documents mentioned at paragraphs 289 (1) to 289 (3) above.
In cases where a person other than a legal heir is named as a beneficiary in the Will, applicable documents must also be obtained from her/ him.
In such cases, an RCB must additionally call for the documents mentioned at paragraphs 289 (4) and 289 (5) above.

296. The standardised forms and other documents required for settlement of claims with respect to the deposit accounts/ safe deposit locker/ articles in safe custody kept by a deceased customer must be made available in all the branches as well as on the RCB’s website for the convenience of the claimant(s).
Further, the RCB must also display on its website, the list of documents to be submitted by a claimant and the procedure to be followed for settlement of claims in various scenarios.

In case all required documents for processing of the claim have been submitted by the claimant, an RCB must also issue a confirmation in this regard.

On subsequent submission of all the required documents, the RCB must issue a confirmation to the claimant that all required documents have been received for processing of the claim.

Upon a claimant uploading the claim form along with the required documents, the RCB must send acknowledgement / confirmation through appropriate channels and also make available the provision for online tracking of the status of the claim.
In such cases, if an RCB requires the claimant to produce original documents for submission / verification, the same must be allowed to be done at any of its branches.

301. If any deposit related claim isn't settled within the timeframe stipulated at paragraph 299 above, then an RCB must communicate the reasons for such delay to the claimant(s).

Further, in cases of delay attributable to the RCB, compensation must be paid by the RCB in the form of interest, at a rate not less than the prevailing Bank Rate + 4% per annum, on the settlement amount due for the period of delay.
The reference date for reckoning the amount due and the prevailing Bank Rate must be the date of receipt of all required documents from the claimant.

302. For claims related to safe deposit locker/ articles in safe custody, an RCB must be required to pay compensation to the claimant(s) at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay, in cases where it doesn’t adhere to the timeline prescribed in paragraph 300 above.
Accordingly, the RCB must follow the procedure for settlement of claims in respect of such accounts as has been prescribed above for the accounts with/ without nominee/ survivorship clause,.
