305. An RCB must continue to spread awareness among its customers about the benefits of the nomination facility/ survivorship clause and give wide publicity to these facilities along with the procedure for settlement of claims.

306. An RCB must transparently disclose to the borrower all information about fees / charges payable for processing the loan application, the amount of fees refundable if loan amount isn't sanctioned / disbursed, pre-payment options and charges, if any, penalty for delayed repayments if any, conversion charges for switching loan from fixed to floating rates or vice versa, existence of any interest reset clause and any other matter which affects the interest of the borrower.
Such information must also be displayed on the website of the RCB, if any, for all categories of loan products.

307. In other words, banks must disclose 'all in cost' inclusive of all such charges involved in processing / sanction of loan application in a transparent manner to enable the customer to compare the rates and charges with other sources of finance.

308. Besides, in case of all categories of loans irrespective of any threshold limits, an RCB must also convey in writing, within stipulated time, the main reasons which, in the opinion of the RCB, have led to rejection of the loan applications.
309. The following instructions must be applicable in all new retail and MSME term loans sanctioned on or after October 1, 2024, including fresh loans to existing customers, by an RCB.

Credit card receivables are exempted from the provisions given below: (1) An RCB must provide a KFS to all prospective borrowers to help them take an informed view before executing the loan contract, as per the standardised format given in the Annex XIII.
The KFS must be written in a language understood by such borrowers.
Contents of KFS must be explained to the borrower and an acknowledgement must be obtained that they have understood the same.

(2) The KFS must be provided with a unique proposal number and must have a validity period of at least three working days for loans having tenor of seven days or more, and a validity period of one working day for loans having tenor of less than seven days.
An RCB must be bound by the terms of the loan indicated in the KFS, if agreed to by the borrower during the validity period.
(3) The KFS must also include a computation sheet of Annual Percentage Rate (APR), and the amortisation schedule of the loan over the loan tenor.

(4) Charges recovered from the borrowers by an RCB on behalf of third-party service providers on actual basis, such as insurance charges, legal charges etc. must also form part of the APR and must be disclosed separately.
In all cases wherever the RCB is involved in recovering such charges, the receipts and related documents must be provided to the borrower for each payment, within a reasonable time.
(6) The KFS must also be included as a summary box to be exhibited as part of the loan agreement.

An RCB must put in place an appropriate policy framework meeting the following requirements for implementation and compliance: (1) At the time of sanction, the RCB must clearly communicate to the borrower about the possible impact of change in benchmark interest rate on the loan leading to changes in EMI and / or tenor or both.
Subsequently, any increase in the EMI / tenor or both on account of the above must be communicated to the borrower immediately through appropriate channels.

(3) The borrowers must also be given the choice to opt for (i) enhancement in EMI or elongation of tenor or for a combination of both options; and, (ii) to prepay, either in part or in full, at any point during the tenor of the loan.
Levy of pre-payment charges must be subject to extant instructions.
Note: Whenever there is a reset of interest rates for an entire class of borrowers in a particular loan category, say home loan, due to increase in the reference benchmark.

(4) All applicable charges for switching of loans from floating to fixed rate and any other service charges / administrative costs incidental to the exercise of the above options must be transparently disclosed in the sanction letter and also at the time of revision of such charges / costs by the RCB when needed.
The applicable charges must be as approved by the Board and must be displayed on the RCB’s website.
(5) The RCB must ensure that the elongation of tenor in case of floating rate loan doesn't result in negative amortisation.

(6) The RCB must share / make accessible to the borrower, through appropriate channels, a statement at the end of each quarter which must at the minimum, enumerate the principal and interest recovered till date, EMI amount, number of EMIs left and annualized rate of interest / APR for the entire tenor of the loan.
The RCB must ensure that the statements are simple and easily understood by the borrower.

311.Apart from the EMI based loans, these instructions must also apply, mutatis mutandis, to all equated instalment-based personal loans of different periodicities irrespective of whether they are linked to an external benchmark or an internal benchmark.
In case of personal loans linked to an external benchmark, the RCB must put in place adequate information systems to monitor transmission of changes in the benchmark rate to the lending rate.
312. In case of existing floating rate term loans sanctioned to individual borrowers on or before December 31, 2025, an RCB must not levy pre-payment charges.
313. An RCB must adhere to the following directions regarding levy of pre-payment charges on loans and advances (term loans as well as demand loans) sanctioned or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.
(1) For all floating rate loans granted for purposes other than business to individuals, with or without co-obligant(s), an RCB must not levy pre-payment charges.

(2) For all floating rate loans with sanctioned amount / limit up to ₹50 lakh granted for business purpose to individuals and Micro and Small Enterprises (as defined in Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006), with or without co-obligant(s), an RCB must not levy pre-payment charges.

(3) The Directions at paragraph 313(1) and 313(2) above must be applicable irrespective of the source of funds used for pre-payment of loans, either in part or in full, and without any minimum lock-in period.
(5) In cases other than those mentioned at paragraphs 313(1) and 313(2) above, pre-payment charges, if any, must be as per the approved policy of the RCB.
However, in case of term loans, pre-payment charges, if levied by the RCB, must be based on the amount being prepaid.
In case of cash credit/ overdraft facilities, pre-payment charges on closure of the facility before the due date must be levied on an amount not exceeding the sanctioned limit.

(6) In case of cash credit / overdraft facilities, no pre-payment charges must be applicable if the borrower intimates the RCB of her / his its intention not to renew the facility before the period as stipulated in the loan agreement, but the facility gets closed on the due date.
(7) An RCB must not levy any charges where pre-payment is effected at the instance of the RCB.
(8) The applicability or otherwise of pre-payment charges must be clearly disclosed in the sanction letter and loan agreement.
Further, in case of loans and advances where KFS is to be provided as specified in paragraph 309 above, the same must also be mentioned in the KFS.
No pre-payment charges which have not been disclosed as specified here must be charged by the RCB.
(9) The RCB must not levy any charges / fees retrospectively at the time of pre-payment of loans, which were waived off earlier by it.

314. An RCB must release all the original movable / immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry within a period of 30 days after full repayment/ settlement of the loan account.

315. The borrower must be given the option of collecting the original movable / immovable property documents either from the banking outlet / branch where the loan account was serviced or any other office of the RCB where the documents are available, as per her / his preference.
316. The timeline and place of return of original movable / immovable property documents must be mentioned in the loan sanction letters issued on or after December 1, 2023.

317. to address the contingent event of demise of the sole borrower or joint borrowers, the RCB must have a well laid out procedure for return of original movable / immovable property documents to the legal heirs.
Such procedure must be displayed on the website of the RCB along with other similar policies and procedures for customer information.

318. An RCB must communicate to the borrower reasons for delay in releasing of original movable / immovable property documents or failing to file charge satisfaction form with relevant registry beyond 30 days after full repayment/ settlement of loan.
In case where the delay is attributable to the RCB, it must compensate the borrower at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay.

319. In case of loss / damage to original movable / immovable property documents, either in part or in full, the RCB must assist the borrower in obtaining duplicate / certified copies of the movable / immovable property documents and must bear the associated costs, in addition to paying compensation as indicated at paragraph 318 above.
Further, the compensation provided under these directions must be without limiting the rights of a borrower to get any other compensation as per any applicable law.
321. An RCB must not insist upon legal representation for release of other assets of deceased borrowers irrespective of the amount involved.
322. The Directions contained under this section must be applicable from April 1, 2026.

323. The policy on lending against gold and silver collateral as required under Reserve Bank of India (Rural Cooperative Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025 (called ‘the policy’ in this Section) / SOPs prepared under the policy must cover the conduct related aspects relating to: (1) assaying procedure of jewellery, ornaments or coins made of gold or silver (“eligible collateral” for this section).

324. An RCB, which provides or intends to provide loans against eligible collateral, must ensure that a standardised procedure is put in place to assay the purity of gold and silver collateral, its weight (gross as well as net), etc. This procedure must be adopted uniformly across all its branches for all assaying procedures.

325. An RCB must display on its website the methodology adopted by it for determination of net weight of the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral and the price used to value the gold and silver content of the eligible collateral for determination of LTV ratio.
326. An RCB must ensure presence of the borrower(s) while assaying the collateral at the time of sanctioning the loan.

The deductions relating to stone weight, fastenings, etc. as part of the assaying procedure must be explained to the borrower(s) and details incorporated in the certificate to be issued as per paragraph 330 below.

327. Post pledging, cases involving loss of gold or silver collateral and any deterioration or discrepancy in quantity or purity observed during internal audit or otherwise including at the time of return or auction of collateral must be recorded and communicated promptly to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).
The process for making reimbursement or compensation as per the policy or SOP must also be communicated to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).
328. Documentation must be standardised across all branches of an RCB.

329. The loan agreement must cover the description of the eligible collateral taken as security; value of such collateral; details of auction procedure and the circumstances leading to the auction of the eligible collateral.
All applicable charges payable by the borrower, including those related to assaying, auction, etc. must be clearly included in the loan agreement and KFS.

330. An RCB, while accepting the eligible collateral, must prepare a certificate or e-certificate in duplicate on its letterhead regarding the assay of the collateral and state in it the purity (under carats); gross weight of the eligible collateral pledged; net weight of gold or silver content in it and deductions, if any, relating to weight of stones, lac, alloy, strings, fastenings, etc. damage, breakage or defects, if any, noticed in the collateral; image of the collateral; and the value of collateral arrived at the time of sanction (as per the instructions on valuation and assaying of Gold and Silver collateral specified in the Reserve Bank of India (Rural Co-operative Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025).
One copy of the certificate or e-certificate must be kept as part of the loan documents.

331. All communication with the borrower, especially, the terms and conditions of the loan, or other important communication which affects the interest of the borrower or the lender, must be in the language of the region or in a language as chosen by the borrower.
For an illiterate borrower, important terms and conditions must be explained in the presence of a witness, who must not be an employee of the RCB.

332. An RCB must ensure that necessary infrastructure and facilities are put in place and appropriate security measures taken in each of its branches where loans are sanctioned against gold and / or silver collateral.
333. An RCB must ensure that the gold and / or silver collateral is handled only in its branches and only by its employees.
334. An RCB must store the collateral only in its branches which are manned by its employees and having safe deposit vaults fit for storing gold and silver.
Normally, such loans must not be extended by branches that don't have appropriate secured facility for storage of the pledged eligible collateral.

336. An RCB must periodically review the adequacy of systems for storage of the eligible collateral, conduct training of the concerned staff and carry out internal audit of all procedures to ensure that these are strictly adhered to.
337. As part of internal audit, an RCB must carry out periodic surprise verification of the gold and silver collateral pledged with it and must maintain a record of it.

A clause in the loan agreement must be included for obtaining consent of the borrower(s) to carry out surprise verification including assay of the pledged eligible collateral even in their absence during the tenor of the loan.
This aspect must be specifically communicated to the borrower at the time of sanctioning the loan.

338. An RCB must release or return the pledged eligible collateral held as security to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) on the same day but in any case, not exceeding a maximum period of seven working days upon full repayment or settlement of the loan.

339. At the time of release of pledged eligible collateral to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s), the collateral must be verified for correctness as per details in the certificate to the borrowers’ satisfaction.
340. An RCB must give adequate notice to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s), through available means of communication to repay or settle the loan dues before initiating the auction procedure.
A copy of the notice and acknowledgement of it must be kept on record in both scenarios.

341. An RCB must implement a transparent auction procedure, which must include, among other things, announcement of the auction to the public by issue of advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and another in a national daily.
342. The pledged eligible collateral must be auctioned by an RCB only through its employee having necessary experience and / or training or an auctioneer empanelled by the RCB as per its policy.

In cases where auctions are conducted by the RCB through its employees, necessary safeguards such as surprise visits by regional / controlling officials on periodic basis, coverage under internal audit, etc. must be put in place.
343. An RCB must declare a reserve price for the gold and silver collateral at the time of auction, which must not be less than 90 per cent of its current value.
But in case auctions fail twice, a reserve price not less than 85 per cent of its current value must be adopted.
344. The first auction must be conducted physically in the same district in which the lending branch is located.
345. As a matter of policy, an RCB or its related parties must not participate in the auctions to ensure that there is no potential conflict of interest.
346. After the auction, an RCB must mandatorily provide full details of the value fetched at the auction and the dues adjusted to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).

The surplus, if any, from the auction of the gold or silver collateral, must be refunded to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) within a maximum period of seven working days from the date of receipt of the full auction proceeds.
347. In case of any damage to the pledged eligible collateral by an RCB during the tenor of loan, the cost of repair must be borne by the lender.

348. In case of loss of the pledged eligible collateral and / or any loss emanating from deterioration or discrepancy in quantity or purity observed during internal audit or otherwise including at the time of return or auction of collateral, an RCB must suitably compensate the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).

349. In case of delay in release of the pledged collateral after full repayment or settlement of loan by the borrower, where reasons for delay are attributable to the RCB, it must compensate the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay beyond the timeline prescribed at paragraph 338 above.
If the delay isn't attributable to the RCB, it must communicate reasons for such delay to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s).

Further, where the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) has not approached the RCB for release of pledged eligible collateral after full repayment or settlement of loan, the RCB must issue periodic reminders to the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) through letters, email or SMS if the email and mobile number are registered with the RCB.
350. The compensation provided under these directions must be without limiting the rights of a borrower / legal heir to get any other compensation as per any applicable law.
351. The pledged gold or silver collateral lying with an RCB beyond two years from the date of full repayment or settlement of loan must be treated as unclaimed.
The RCB must periodically undertake special drives to ascertain the whereabouts of the borrower(s) / legal heir(s) in respect of such unclaimed gold and / or silver collateral.
352. A report on unclaimed gold and silver collateral must be put up to the Customer Service Committee or the Board, at half-yearly intervals for a review.
353. An RCB must refrain from issuance of misleading advertisements containing unrealistic claims to promote loans against gold or silver collateral.

354. An RCB must ensure that all arrangements for sourcing and/ or recovery of loans against eligible collateral, are in compliance with applicable directions on outsourcing and recovery practices issued by the Reserve Bank.

355. For prudential related aspects, the RCB must be guided by the instructions contained in the Chapter on ‘Lending against Gold and Silver Collateral’ in Reserve Bank of India (Rural Cooperative Banks – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
356. A Fair Practices Code (FPC) based on these directions must be put in place by an RCB with the approval of its Board.
The FPC must be displayed by the RCB in all its branches and on its website.
The FPC must be issued in a language understood by the borrower.
357. There must be a standard form of loan agreement for microfinance loans in a language understood by the borrower.
358. An RCB must provide a loan card to the borrower which must incorporate the following: (1) Information which adequately identifies the borrower.
359. All entries in the loan card must be in a language understood by the borrower.
360. Issuance of non-credit products must be with full consent of the borrowers and fee structure for such products must be explicitly communicated to the borrower in the loan card itself.
361. There must be no pre-payment charge levied on microfinance loans.
Charges, if any, for delayed payment must be applied on the overdue amount and not on the entire loan amount.

362. An RCB must prominently display the minimum, maximum and average interest rates charged on microfinance loans in all its offices, in the literature (information booklets/ pamphlets) issued by it and details on its website.
This information must also be included in the supervisory returns and subjected to supervisory scrutiny.
363. Any change in interest rate or any other charge must be informed to the borrower well in advance.
365. Reserve Bank must also make available information regarding interest charged by RCBs on microfinance loans.
366. An RCB must have a board approved policy regarding the conduct of employees and system for their recruitment, training and monitoring.
This policy must, among other things, lay down minimum qualifications for the staff and must provide necessary training tools to deal with the customers.
Training to employees must include programs to inculcate appropriate behaviour towards customers.
Conduct of employees towards customers must also be incorporated appropriately in their compensation matrix.
367. Field staff must be trained to make necessary enquiries regarding the income and existing debt of the household.
368. Training, if any, offered to the borrowers must be free of cost.

369. An RCB must put in place a mechanism for identification of the borrowers facing repayment related difficulties, engagement with such borrowers and providing them necessary guidance about the recourse available.
370. Recovery must be made at a designated / central designated place decided mutually by the borrower and the RCB.

However, field staff must be allowed to make recovery at the place of residence or work of the borrower if the borrower fails to appear at the designated / central designated place on two or more successive occasions.
371. An RCB or its agent must not engage in any harsh methods towards recovery.
Without limiting the general application of the foregoing, following practices must be deemed as harsh: (1) Use of threatening or abusive language.
372.An RCB must have a dedicated mechanism for redressal of recovery related grievances.
The details of this mechanism must be provided to the borrower at the time of loan disbursal.
374. An RCB must have a due diligence process in place for engagement of recovery agents, which must, among other things, cover individuals involved in the recovery process.
The RCB must ensure that the recovery agents engaged by them carry out verification of the antecedents of its employees, which must include police verification.
The RCB must also decide the periodicity at which re-verification of antecedents must be resorted to.
375. To ensure due notice and appropriate authorisation, an RCB must provide the details of recovery agents to the borrower while initiating the process of recovery.
The agent must also carry a copy of the notice and the authorisation letter from the RCB along with the identity card issued to her / him by the RCB or the agency.

Further, where the recovery agency is changed by the RCB during the recovery process, in addition to the RCB notifying the borrower of the change, the new agent must carry the notice and the authorisation letter along with her / his identity card.
376. The notice and the authorisation letter must, among other details, also include the contact details of the recovery agency and the RCB.
377. The up-to-date details of the recovery agencies engaged by an RCB must also be hosted on the RCB’s website.

378. An RCB must strictly ensure that it or its agents don't resort to intimidation or harassment of any kind, either verbal or physical, against any person in their debt collection efforts, including acts intended to humiliate publicly or intrude upon the privacy of the debtors' family members, referees and friends, sending inappropriate messages either on mobile or through social media, making threatening and / or anonymous calls, persistently calling the borrower and/ or calling the borrower before 8:00 a.m.
379. Standing instructions must be freely accepted on all current and savings bank accounts.
The scope of standing instructions service must be expanded to include payments on account of taxes, rents, bills, school / college fees, licences, etc. B.
Fractions of 50 paise and above must be rounded off to the next higher rupee and fraction of less than 50 paise must be ignored.
However, an RCB must ensure that cheques / drafts issued by clients containing fractions of a rupee aren't rejected or dishonoured by it.
The RCB must ensure that appropriate action is taken against members of its staff who are found to have refused to accept cheques / drafts containing fractions of a rupee.
384. An RCB must extend necessary help / co-ordination to tax officials whenever required.
Further, the RCB must treat with utmost seriousness cases where its staff connive / assist in any manner with offences punishable under the Income Tax Act.
In such cases, in addition to the normal criminal action, such staff member must also be proceeded against departmentally.
All approvals or acknowledgments granted under these repealed lists must be deemed as governed by these Directions.
